name: Harriet Hageman

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL FRAUD ENFORCEMENT DIVISION ACT OF 2026
statements.title: NATIONAL FRAUD ENFORCEMENT DIVISION ACT OF 2026
sentences: But before going to my specific remarks, I would just like to note that you can tell when my friends on the other side of the aisle start to panic because you start hearing them scream at the top of their lungs: ``Trump, Epstein,'' and all the other things, as they try to deflect attention from what is an excellent bill that should be passed by this body.
Madam Speaker, waste, fraud, and abuse persist in nearly every sector across this Nation, including healthcare, public welfare programs, foreign aid, and the issuance of commercial driver's licenses.

My colleagues across the aisle emphasize the importance of programs like Medicaid and SNAP, but allowing waste, fraud, and abuse to continue unaddressed redirects funding away from the populations they are intended to assist, while threatening the programs' fiscal stability.

The Department of Justice created the National Fraud Enforcement Division earlier this year for precisely these reasons, fulfilling a vital mission of the department, while bolstering cooperation between Federal, State, local, and Tribal law enforcement.
Last week, a man in California was sent to prison for his role in a healthcare fraud scheme in which nearly $270 million in fraudulent claims were submitted to the California Medicaid program.

Just yesterday, it was announced that 12 individuals are facing Federal fraud charges after it was found that over $10 million intended to help low-income families and pay for childcare was funneled to fraudulent daycare providers.
Madam Speaker, I rise today in strong support of H.R. 9576, the National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026.
I urge all of my colleagues, including the Democrats, to support H.R. 9576.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 9576, NATIONAL FRAUD ENFORCEMENT DIVISION ACT OF 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 10326, PREVENTING RIP-OFFS AND OBTAIN
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 9576, NATIONAL FRAUD ENFORCEMENT DIVISION ACT OF 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 10326, PREVENTING RIP-OFFS AND OBTAINING OVERSIGHT OF FUNDS ACT...
sentences: If this rule passes, the House will be able to terminate two more California Clean Air Act waivers approved by the EPA.
The Clean Air Act, which codifies Federal jurisdiction over emissions, preempts all State emission standards.
It can develop its own emissions standards and request a waiver that the EPA must approve, subject to limited disqualifying conditions.
First, section 177 of the Clean Air Act allows other States to adopt these California standards, which 17 States and the District of Columbia have done.

This subjects Wyoming to California law, undermining our State authorities and Federal law to subject us to climate lunacy policies with devastating consequences for consumer choice, safety, and prices.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of House Resolution 1530.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all of my colleagues to support House Resolution 1530 and the underlying legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO THE CONSTITUTION OF THE UNITED STATES TO REQUIRE THAT THE SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES BE COMPOSED OF NINE JUSTICES
statements.title: PROPOSING AN AMENDMENT TO THE CONSTITUTION OF THE UNITED STATES TO REQUIRE THAT THE SUPREME COURT OF THE UNITED STATES BE COMPOSED OF NINE JUSTICES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of H.J. Res. 1, proposing a constitutional amendment to maintain nine Justices on the United States Supreme Court.

The composition of the Supreme Court has consistently been maintained at nine members for over 150 years, a period of time during which the Court issued some of its most important constitutional jurisprudence.
We must remember that the Supreme Court is the final arbiter of all cases and controversies arising under the Constitution.
In recent years, however, and as the Supreme Court has correctly returned to its originalist roots, there are many on the left who have sought to politicize the Court.
Their solution to losing these constitutional legal arguments isn't to seek to change the law but to attack the Supreme Court and threaten to pack it with judicial advocates.

Calls for packing the Supreme Court, whether it be from FDR over half a century ago or from elected Democrat officials in the 21st century, are designed to do one of two things: threaten and hold the Court hostage to control its decisions or to load it with political actors so as to change its nature entirely.
Mr. Speaker, I thank Representative Biggs and Chairman Jordan for their leadership on this legislation, and I urge all of my colleagues to support H.J. Res. 1.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
sentences: I commend Chairman Diaz-Balart for his bold leadership to reform U.S. foreign aid over the last several funding cycles.
This bill puts forward a second consecutive year of spending cuts, counters the global climate lunacy agenda, and holds rogue U.N. agencies accountable.
Since 2023, the U.N. has been setting the stage for nations to sue one another for violations of climate change treaties, with the spoils of these lawsuits being for so-called climate reparations.
This bill aligns with legislation I have introduced to block climate reparations.
Secondly, Washington, D.C., has turned a blind eye to the Chinese Communist Party's infiltration of the United Nations, with our taxpayer dollars being used to fund the CCP's malign influence agenda.
Mr. Chair, I rise today in strong support of H.R. 8595, the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICA CELEBRATING 250 YEARS
statements.title: AMERICA CELEBRATING 250 YEARS
sentences: Self-Reflection to Self-Hatred Mr. Speaker, our 250-year quest to become a more perfect union has always involved asking hard questions and self-reflection: How do we fulfill the promises of our founding documents in the context of governing this vast country from east to west and north to south?
We tore our country apart with the Union fighting to abolish slavery from our shores.

Unlike the other countries around the world who had slavery or continue to practice it to this day, we endured the exorcism of a Civil War, and we emerged to secure a stronger, more equal, more just, and more determined union.
These weaponized emotions threaten to divide us further and represent yet another obstacle to conquer on our crusade to deliver a more perfect union.
We are proud to be the home of the Northern Arapahoe Tribe and the Eastern Shoshone Tribe of the Wind River Indian Reservation, whose cultures and traditions have enriched our cultural history.
When they brought me home from the hospital, they had just recently bought a ranch, were over $200,000 in debt in 1962, and had $35 in the bank.
I had brilliant and compassionate educators who taught me to think and presented we with the rich mosaic of the real world so I could succeed in the real world.
Farmers, builders, artists, intellectuals, gold miners, businessowners, dreamers, second sons, and even some storied outlaws moved West to claim their future in the new frontier.
In the 1860s, the Gettysburg flag waved among the unbearable noise of wars as our ancestors fought to keep the Union together and abolish slavery.

Our achievements are like the scope and size of the universe barely scratched by the Artemis program: They are simply too great for us to fully appreciate unless we are willing to actually study who we are, what makes us different, why America has succeeded as a beacon of hope and renewal, and why we must fight every day to make sure that the next 250 years are even more spectacular than the last.

On July Fourth, we will be celebrating our collective birthday, and I am honored to stand on the floor of the United States House of Representatives, in this beautiful Capitol, in this glorious and dynamic city, to describe what that means to me, the lone Representative of the least populated State in our country.
I hope that by focusing on America's 250th anniversary and looking back over our history with honesty and accuracy, we will reverse these declines.
This does not mean that we reject other cultures or traditions.

What better time to celebrate our history, culture, and traditions than on this 250th anniversary, being optimistic that in 2026, while looking both backwards and forwards since Ronald Reagan professed it to be ``morning again in America,'' we will realize that it is a bright, golden sunrise shining over the new horizons of a novel American Pax Romana, the dawn of a truly golden age of America.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CHALLENGING CLIMATE SHAKEDOWNS
statements.title: CHALLENGING CLIMATE SHAKEDOWNS
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to expose and challenge the climate shakedowns at the root of increasing energy costs being imposed on every American.
So-called climate Superfund laws have cropped up in nearly a dozen leftist States, punishing those who harvest the very product that has fueled America's unrivaled prosperity.
Make no mistake: War with Iran is not the cause of our energy struggle.
I ask my colleagues to pass the Stop Climate Shakedowns Act to protect our producers immediately.
We will need them now more than ever as America continues to grow, and demand for quality food products increases.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS 2ND AMENDMENT PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: VETERANS 2ND AMENDMENT PROTECTION ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of H.R. 1041, the Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act because I do, in fact, care about our veterans.

For three decades, the Department of Veterans Affairs has abided by the misguided policy that a veteran's fiduciary status alone, absent any judicial order, is grounds to report such a veteran to the FBI's National Instant Criminal Background Check System.
It not only infringes on the Second Amendment rights of our veterans, but it also strips them of their due process protections, which are afforded to every other American citizen.

With over 40,000 veterans across Wyoming, ensuring that we are permanently restoring the Second Amendment rights for each of them is of paramount importance to me, and that is precisely what this bill will do.
I want to thank Chairman Bost and the House Veterans' Affairs Committee for their tireless leadership on this critical issue, and I urge all my colleagues to support H.R. 1041.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONWIDE CONSUMER AND FUEL RETAILER CHOICE ACT OF 2025
statements.title: NATIONWIDE CONSUMER AND FUEL RETAILER CHOICE ACT OF 2025
sentences: This bill is not in line with the values we support as Republicans such as free and fair markets.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FIRE IMPROVEMENT AND REFORMING EXCEPTIONAL EVENTS ACT
statements.title: FIRE IMPROVEMENT AND REFORMING EXCEPTIONAL EVENTS ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 6387 to ensure States are not unjustly penalized under the Clean Air Act for engaging in responsible, proactive wildfire mitigation activities.

Unfortunately, as it currently stands under the Clean Air Act, the use of these individual wildfire mitigation measures can create uncertainty, discouraging their use out of concern that doing so would lead to noncompliance with National Ambient Air Quality Standards.

By reforming the Clean Air Act to ensure these wildfire mitigation activities are appropriately treated as exceptional events, we are incentivizing their use and putting a stop to unfair and counterproductive regulatory punishments.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBE LEASING AUTHORITY
statements.title: FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBE LEASING AUTHORITY
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of my bill, H.R. 5910, which amends the Long-Term Leasing Act to authorize any federally recognized Indian Tribe to lease land held in trust for its benefit for up to 99 years.
With the enactment of the Indian Nonintercourse Act in 1834, Tribal land transactions have generally required congressional authorization.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: VETERANS ACCESSIBILITY ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACT OF 2025
statements.title: VETERANS ACCESSIBILITY ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of S. 1383, the SAVE America Act, which I am proud to cosponsor and hope will pass the House floor today.
The SAVE America Act requires individuals to provide documented proof of U.S. citizenship along with a valid photo ID when registering to vote.
This commonsense legislation strengthens election integrity through practical measures, including voter ID requirements and safeguards to prevent noncitizens from voting.
The SAVE America Act is particularly important as we continue to address the consequences of the Biden-Harris border crisis, which led to millions of individuals entering the country unlawfully.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to join me in voting in favor of the SAVE America Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REPEAL OF SENATE NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO LEGAL PROCESS ON DISCLOSURES OF SENATE DATA
statements.title: REPEAL OF SENATE NOTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS RELATING TO LEGAL PROCESS ON DISCLOSURES OF SENATE DATA
sentences: Included in the Senate amendment to H.R. 5371 was a section providing for a private right of action for those Senators who were targeted by the Biden administration to access their cell phone data.

The Senators, similar to any other citizen who was wrongfully targeted by the Biden administration, already have a private right of action to sue the Federal Government, including the FBI and other agencies that may have been involved, for violation of their Fourth Amendment rights and other statutory provisions that govern privacy rights and/or that limit Federal law enforcement from pursuing political witch hunts.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 6019.

I support repealing this particular provision, not because I think that these Senators and others should not be able to sue the Federal Government for these acts, but because they already have the ability to do so.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "BUFFALO FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RES
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "BUFFALO FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN AMENDMENT"
sentences: The Biden RMP is instead very clearly a mineral withdrawal enacted by climate activists in direct violation of the law.

The Biden administration's decision to terminate mining in Wyoming's PRB is not only irresponsible and harmful but downright illegal, a mechanism used by the governing elite to inflict harm on every single citizen of this great country to further climate change lunacy.
With coal generating as much as 23 percent of America's electricity at any given time, Wyoming coal supplies as much as 9.2 percent of the electricity produced in this country.

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of my legislation, H.J. Res. 130, which utilizes the congressional disapproval procedure under the Congressional Review Act, or CRA, to restore coal leasing in Wyoming's Powder River Basin.
I urge all of my colleagues to vote in favor of H.J. Res. 130.

statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT RELATING TO "MILES CITY FIELD OFFICE RECORD OF DECISION AND APPROVED RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PLAN...

To this day, I am still baffled and horrified that, for 4 years, our government intentionally tried to impose energy poverty on the American people, all to please the vocal but minority climate lobby.
